chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Husayn Al-Hashimi, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq Al-Ahmar, and Ali ibn Bundar, from As-Sayyari, from some of the Baghdadi, from Ali ibn Bilal, who said:

Hisham ibn Al-Hakam met some of the Khawarij, who said to him: 'O Hisham, what do you say about the Ajam (non-Arabs) marrying into the Arabs?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And do the Arabs marry into Quraysh?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'And do Quraysh marry into Banu Hashim?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'From whom did you take this?' He said: 'From Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him). I heard him saying: "Your bloods are equal, but your genitals (marital eligibility) are not equal."'

The Kharijite went out until he came to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said: 'I met Hisham and asked him about such and such, and he informed me with such and such, and mentioned that he heard it from you.' He (the Imam) said: 'Yes, I have said that.'

The Kharijite said: 'Here I am, I have come to you as a suitor.' Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'You are indeed equal to me in your nobility and lineage among your people, but Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, protected us from As-Sadaqah (marriage of convenience/intermarriage for status), which is the dross of people's hands. He disliked that we share in what Allah favored us with with someone whom Allah did not make equal to us in what He gave us.'

The Kharijite stood up while saying: 'By Allah, I have never seen a man like him, and by Allah, He rejected me with the ugliest rejection, and he did not deviate from the statement of his companion (Hisham).

key_terms.بَنِي هَاشِمٍ: Banu Hashim (the clan of the Prophet)
key_terms.تَتَكَافَى دِمَاؤُكُمْ: Your bloods are equal (referring to lineage)
key_terms.قُرَيْشٍ: Quraysh (the tribe of the Prophet Muhammad)

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on marriage equality (kafa'ah) between the Ahl al-Bayt and others?
ai.summary: This hadith, found in Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, elucidates the Shia jurisprudential distinction between social equality and the specific spiritual-ontological status of the Ahl al-Bayt. While the Kharijite correctly cites Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) that 'bloods are equal' (referring to general human lineage), the Imam clarifies that divine selection ('Al-Ishtiraf') creates a unique barrier for the Imams, who are protected from marrying those not granted equal divine favor. This establishes 'Kafa'ah' not merely as tribal parity but as a reflection of the Imam's elevated, divinely ordained status.
